books.section: Topic 1.4 Columbian Exchange, Spanish Exploration, and Conquest
The Early Colonial Era: Spain Colonizes the New World

primary_sources: Florentine Codex, Book 12, c. 1585, public domain

options.text: Spanish guns and steel were too few in number and too weak to matter in battle.
options.misconception: Guns and steel did matter; they gave small Spanish forces an edge. They were not decisive on their own.

options.text: Native peoples refused to fight the Spanish invaders and gave up without a battle.
options.misconception: Native peoples fought hard; Tenochtitlan's defenders held the city for months under siege.

options.text: Epidemics struck the Americas only after the conquests were already complete.
options.misconception: The order is wrong: smallpox hit Tenochtitlan during the 1520 siege, before the city fell.

options.text: Native peoples had no immunity to Old World diseases, separated from those germs for thousands of years.

rationales.A: Guns and steel did help the Spanish win battles. But a few hundred soldiers could not have conquered empires of millions without the epidemics that broke those empires first.
rationales.B: The record shows the opposite. The Mexica defended Tenochtitlan for months, and the Inca fought on for years after Pizarro took Atahualpa.
rationales.C: The timing is backwards. Smallpox reached Tenochtitlan in 1520, during the siege, and killed the emperor Cuitlahuac before the city fell.
rationales.D: The Americas had been separated from the germs of Europe, Africa, and Asia for thousands of years. When smallpox, measles, and influenza arrived, no one had any resistance, so the dying went far beyond anything weapons alone could do.
rationales.general:
1. Compare the two candidates. A few hundred Spaniards had steel and guns; millions of Native people faced them.
2. Ask what broke the empires. Epidemics killed a huge share of the population, including leaders, before and during the fighting.
3. Ask why the epidemics were so deadly. The Americas had been cut off from Old World germs for thousands of years, so no one had immunity.
4. Rule out the rest. Weapons mattered and Native peoples fought hard, but neither explains the speed of the collapse.
Remember: when a small force conquers fast, look for the invisible cause that did the most damage.

stem: Historians debate why the Spanish conquered the Aztec and Inca empires so quickly. Which factor best explains why disease, rather than Spanish weapons, is usually ranked as the most important cause?

stimulus.source_note: Florentine Codex, Book 12, c. 1585, public domain, Wikimedia Commons. Image viewed before writing.
stimulus.text: This drawing from the Florentine Codex, Book 12, shows Nahua people suffering from smallpox in central Mexico in the 1500s. On the left, a sick person covered in spots lies on a mat while another person leans over them. On the right, bodies covered in spots lie still on woven mats, unable to move.
